hero.title: Dental implants
hero.lead: An implant replaces the root of a missing tooth and supports a new tooth on top. It’s fixed in place, so there’s nothing to take out at night.

intro.heading: How an implant replaces a tooth
intro.html:
A dental implant has three parts: a post placed in the jawbone that acts as the root, a connector called an abutment, and a crown that looks like a natural tooth. Over the healing period, the bone bonds to the implant, giving it a strong foundation.

Implants can replace a single tooth, several teeth, or support a bridge or denture.
intro.aside_heading: People often ask about implants when
aside: A tooth has been lost or needs to come out
A bridge would mean preparing healthy neighbouring teeth
Dentures feel loose and they want more security
They want a fixed replacement that doesn’t come out

callout.title: Start with a complimentary implant consultation
callout.html: Your dentist checks whether implants suit you and talks you through your plan and costs. Dr Alex and Dr Louie both have a particular interest in implant dentistry. Meet our dentists

explain.heading: Is an implant right for you?
explain.intro: Implants aren’t suitable for everyone. Your general health, the bone in your jaw and the condition of your other teeth all play a part. If an implant isn’t the best fit, your dentist will talk you through alternatives such as a bridge or dentures, including implant-retained dentures.

process.heading: Three stages, planned around you
process.intro: Timing differs between patients. Your dentist will give you a plan for your own treatment.
steps: Your dentist checks whether implants suit you and talks you through a treatment plan and costs. A mould of your teeth and a special 3D X-ray are taken before the next stage.
The implant is placed into the jawbone under local anaesthetic.
Once the implant has healed into the bone, your new tooth is fitted on top.

weigh.heading: Benefits and things to consider
benefits: Fixed in place, without relying on neighbouring teeth
Looks and functions much like a natural tooth
consider: Involves minor surgery and a healing period of months
Enough healthy bone is needed, and some people need extra procedures
Smoking, gum disease and some health conditions can affect success
Implants need daily cleaning and regular reviews, just like teeth
alternatives: Leaving the gap, after discussing the effect on your bite

care.heading: Looking after your implant
items: Follow your dentist’s instructions on eating, cleaning and pain relief while the area heals.
Brush and clean around the implant as carefully as your natural teeth.
Regular check-ups help keep the gum and bone around the implant healthy.

faqs: Am I too old for implants?
Age alone isn’t usually the deciding factor. Your general health, bone and gums matter more. Your dentist will assess this at a consultation.
It varies. After the implant is placed, healing often takes around three months before the permanent tooth is fitted, and some cases take longer.
cost: Implant costs vary with the number of implants, the type of crown and any extra procedures. Your dentist will give you a written plan with costs after your consultation.
